question: Would any accuracy gain from the context regime be attributable to the context itself rather than to the model seeing more tokens/triples or more training signal per example?
description: The natural control is matched supervision budget: equal number of examples AND equal token budget, with the isolated regime given unrelated/random triples of the same length. Without this, gains are uninterpretable.
confidence_basis: Based on four directly relevant retrieved papers with verbatim quotes (IKG/KGSweetSpot, Lost in the Middle, Never Lost in the Middle) plus the DrKGC and SG-RAG MOT contradiction; the specific matched-budget training-time experiment has not been run by anyone in the retrieved set, so the conclusion is about experimental design rather than a measured KGQA result.
rationale: This is the single most likely way the main effect could be an artifact, and it directly determines whether the contribution is defensible.
resolution: Partially resolved, and reframed. Evidence shows the confounder is real but is not fundamentally about token counts: (i) imprecise selection of KG knowledge can push performance below the no-context zero-shot baseline, and expanding subgraph scope raises recall while lowering precision (C015, C016, IKG/KGSweetSpot); (ii) language models use long contexts non-uniformly, with significant degradation depending on the position of relevant information (C017, Lost in the Middle); (iii) how well a model uses supplied context is itself trainable (C018, Never Lost in the Middle). Meanwhile no retrieved work runs a matched-example, matched-token comparison of training-time context supervision with an equal-length irrelevant-context arm (C019). Therefore a token-matched comparison alone would still leave the attribution ambiguous; the experiment must include an equal-length irrelevant/random-triples arm and a relevance-selection condition, and treat B-vs-C (relevant vs. equal-length irrelevant context) as the primary contrast. Verification remaining: run the factorial study; no KGQA paper in the searched set reports this comparison.
